options: A 'graph of metadata' that defines the structure, schema and semantics of a knowledge graph within a graph database
A chart that plots the size of a database over time
A relational table that stores graph images
A machine learning model trained on graphs
A backup copy of a knowledge graph
questions.explanation: A MetaGraph is the 'graph about the graph', providing information about the structure, schema and semantics of a knowledge graph.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the things a MetaGraph specifies as a conceptual framework?
options: Entity types, such as Person, Company or Product
The actual data instance of every customer record
Relationship types, such as Works For or Buys
Attributes of nodes and edges, such as Name or Date
Constraints, such as cardinality and mandatory fields
questions.explanation: A MetaGraph specifies entity types, relationship types, attributes and constraints; the actual data instances belong to the knowledge graph itself.

questions.stem: How does a MetaGraph relate to a knowledge graph?
options: The MetaGraph replaces the knowledge graph
The knowledge graph is a smaller copy of the MetaGraph
The MetaGraph serves as the blueprint that defines the structure, schema and semantics of the knowledge graph's relationships
The two are unrelated technologies
The knowledge graph stores the metadata and the MetaGraph stores the data
questions.explanation: While knowledge graphs represent relationships between entities, a MetaGraph is the blueprint defining the structure, schema and semantics of those relationships.

questions.stem: Which reason for a MetaGraph's importance refers to ensuring the knowledge graph adheres to a well-defined schema and preventing inconsistent or ambiguous relationships?
options: Data discovery
Performance optimisation
Interoperability
Semantic integrity
Scalability
questions.explanation: Semantic integrity is the MetaGraph's role in ensuring that the knowledge graph adheres to a well-defined schema, preventing inconsistent or ambiguous relationships.

questions.stem: How does a MetaGraph support interoperability?
options: By converting all graphs into relational tables
By deleting duplicate nodes automatically
By encrypting edges between systems
By requiring every graph to use the same vendor
By acting as a universal schema to integrate multiple knowledge graphs, enabling seamless data exchange
questions.explanation: A MetaGraph can act as a universal schema that integrates multiple knowledge graphs, enabling seamless data exchange.

questions.stem: Which MetaGraph component covers inheritance hierarchies, cardinality rules and restrictions such as 'a Company can have multiple Employees but not vice versa'?
options: Graph Schema Rules
Node Classes
Edge Classes
Attribute Metadata
Entity Instances
questions.explanation: Graph Schema Rules include inheritance hierarchies, cardinality rules and restrictions on how entities may relate.

questions.stem: In a MetaGraph, what do Edge Classes define?
options: The data types and value ranges of properties
Types of relationships, such as FriendOf, EmployeeOf or PartOf
The types of entities and their attributes
The physical storage location of the graph
The colour used to draw each node
questions.explanation: Edge Classes define types of relationships such as FriendOf, EmployeeOf or PartOf, whereas Node Classes represent types of entities.

questions.stem: Which benefit of a MetaGraph relates to better management of data lineage, compliance and security through clear metadata definitions?
options: Enhanced query capabilities
Scalability
Data governance
Performance overhead
Automated MetaGraph generation
questions.explanation: With clear metadata definitions, a MetaGraph supports data governance by helping organisations manage data lineage, compliance and security.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a challenge in implementing a MetaGraph?
options: Too few use cases for graph databases
Inability to represent constraints
Lack of support for entity types
The absence of a universal standard for MetaGraphs, which can create interoperability issues
Graph databases cannot store metadata
questions.explanation: The challenges named are complexity, performance overhead and standardisation: there is no universal MetaGraph standard, which can create interoperability issues.

questions.stem: In the MetaGraph description, what is the MetaGraph said to enable in terms of representing reality?
options: A replacement for all relational databases
The elimination of ontologies and taxonomies
A guarantee of zero data errors
A ban on unstructured data
A complete digital twin of simple to complex reality
questions.explanation: MetaGraph is described as an enabler for a complete digital twin of simple to complex reality, providing rich context to data across functions and systems.
